name: Forgotten Standard Bearer

Buffs lesser Hollow enemies and creates denial zones.
shortBackstory: Forgotten Standard Bearer is a non-playable Forgotten Remnant whose origin makes Storm-Oath Covenant visible as living battlefield danger.

chapters.title: Origin
chapters.text: Forgotten Standard Bearer remains from a removed war whose civilization cannot be safely restored. It is not a faction citizen and should never read like a recruitable Deity. Its existence proves that the Gate crisis produces consequences, predators, remnants, and catastrophes beyond civilized armies.

chapters.title: Lore Function
chapters.text: As a Forgotten Remnant from Forgotten, Forgotten carries a specific warning into the story: A remnant of a removed civilization whose name cannot be safely spoken. It carries a banner that remembers wars the Codex refuses to restore. This makes the creature useful as canon pressure, not random enemy dressing.

chapters.title: Battlefield Behavior
chapters.text: On the map, Forgotten supports its lore through behavior: Buffs lesser Hollow enemies and creates denial zones. Its abilities — Banner of Loss, Command the Nameless, Memory Cleave — should feel like the environment and story acting through a threat body.

chapters.title: Campaign Tie
chapters.text: In Storm-Oath Covenant, Forgotten connects to the banner-memory pressure that returns during Asgardian Elite remixes. Encounter designers can place it where the player needs to feel what the Gate has damaged: memory, structure, instinct, oath, water, stone, or command.

chapters.title: Visual / Reading Rule
chapters.text: The creature page must preserve the distinction between Deities, NPCs, and non-playable threats. Forgotten can be studied under Creatures and Backstories, but its profile should reinforce danger, not companionship.

developmentStatus: Readable creature profile integrated into dashboard threat pages.
